title: Miniature proxy runtime axioms (personal scratchpad)
content:
Notes-to-self / running journal for the tiny local proxy runtime idea. Aim: a low-complexity runtime that lives on user device or a tiny edge runner to provide prewarm/prefetch, local KV cache, and cheap fallback routing when primary Redwood endpoints are slow. This is a personal sketch — lots of TODOs and half-baked decisions below.

Overview hypothesis:
- Most UX wins come from masking cold-start latency and avoiding round-trips for small deterministic operations (e.g., prompt template expansion, tokenization, short completion).
- A small proxy that understands request fingerprints, simple priors, and a per-session cache can reduce tokens + latency with minimal model instrumentation.

Core axioms (design constraints):
1) Minimal trust surface: proxy never stores permanent PII; ephemeral session keys only.
2) Observable behaviour: every local decision emits a lightweight span/event so service telemetry can calculate hit-rate and fallout.
3) Config-first: runtime behaviour driven by a compact config schema (below) so server-side rollouts can change heuristics.
4) Graceful degradation: when local state is missing or stale, proxy must forward without mutation.
5) Deterministic and idempotent prefetch ops where possible to avoid charging customers for repeated work.

Sketch: config schema (human-friendly pseudo-JSON)
---
config: {
  "version": "1",
  "prefetch": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_parallel": 2,
    "credit_window_ms": 2000,
    "heuristics": ["recent-prefix", "session-popularity"]
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "ttl_ms": 600000,
    "max_entries": 1024,
    "eviction": "lru"
  },
  "routing": {
    "primary": "hosted:api.redwood.ai/v1",
    "fallback": "edge-runner-local",
    "allow_offline": false
  },
  "telemetry": { "sample_rate": 0.05, "emit_local_stats": true }
}
---
Notes on fields: credit_window_ms is how long we allow speculative prefetch credits to be held before being consumed/returned. session-popularity uses a tiny sketch of most-requested prompts in this session to bias prefetch.

API shapes (edges) — lightweight HTTP/JSON shapes we expect client apps to call the proxy with. Keep shapes minimal to encourage adoption.

1) POST /v1/pp/handshake
  body: { client_id, device_info, ephemeral_key_pub, desired_features: ["prefetch","kv-cache"] }
  returns: { ephemeral_key, session_id, prewarm_policy }

2) POST /v1/pp/infer  (proxied call)
  headers: Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_key>
  body: { session_id, prompt, max_tokens, cost_hint, sticky: bool }
  proxy behaviour: 
    - compute fingerprint = hash(prompt + cost_hint + sticky)
    - check kv_cache for fingerprint -> if hit and fresh: return cached_response + telem:hit
    - otherwise forward to primary according to routing policy; mark speculative prefetch credits as used if exists

3) POST /v1/pp/prefetch (advisory)
  body: { session_id, prompt_variant, priority, ttl_hint_ms }
  semantics: best-effort. Accepts and queues prefetch; will not charge user directly if dropped.

Sequence diagram (ASCII):

Client -> LocalProxy: handshake (w/ ephemeral pubkey)
Client -> LocalProxy: infer request #1 (short)
LocalProxy -> KV: miss -> LocalProxy -> HostedAPI: infer request
HostedAPI -> LocalProxy: response (cacheable)
LocalProxy -> Client: response (fast for subsequent identical requests)
Client -> LocalProxy: prefetch for next prompt bundle (low priority)
LocalProxy -> LocalProxy: schedule background prefetch using credit window

ASCII map:
[Client]--(1)-->[Proxy: small vm]
[Proxy]--(2)-->[Hosted API (redwood)] or [Edge Runner] depending on routing policy
   |
   +- [Local KV Cache] (lookups + event emit)

Open design questions / friction points (brain dump):
- Ephemeral key lifecycle: how to rotate with minimal UX friction? refresh every 24h? per-session?
- Billing and audit: speculative prefetches might incur cost. Need a credit ledger and explicit markers so downstream billing can disambiguate speculative vs user-driven requests. (linked: JIRA-PRX-98)
- Failure semantics: if proxy returns cached but slightly stale content, how to signal confidence to client UI so it can show a spinner while validating? add response.confidence field?
- Local storage limits: mobile devices may evict cache unpredictably. Should we allow a "graceful stale hit" window and automatic background refresh?
- Security: prevent prompt-injection via local templates. Proxy should not execute user-supplied tool calls; only forward.

Telemetry / metrics to emit (minimal):
- prefetch_attempts / prefetch_success_rate
- kv_hit_rate (per session, aggregated)
- speculative_credit_balance (gauge)
- forwarded_requests_by_route (hosted / edge / fallback)
- local_decision_latencies (histogram)

Operational playbook notes (quick):
- Rollout: begin disabled for 5% of users, measure kv_hit_rate and perceived latency improvement (client-side A/B hooks).
- Safety rollback knob: server-side config to toggle prefetch and cache TTLs without client update.

Implementation quick wins (MVP):
- tiny rust binary (~10MB) with embedded sqlite for kv cache + minimal HTTP server
- config pulled at handshake time, cached for 1h
- simple credit ledger in-memory with periodic sync to host (every 30s) for reconciliation

Todo (priority):
- [ ] write simple integration test for fingerprint collision behaviour
- [ ] spec billing markers for speculative prefetch (schema + example)
- [ ] prototype handshake rotation and refresh semantics (local + server)
- [ ] small perf test on Pixel 4 and iPhone SE (latency + cold start)
- [ ] mock telemetry pipeline (span tags: proxy.hit, proxy.miss, proxy.prefetch)

Random notes / heuristics I like:
- Favor tiny, predictable caches rather than large LRU that causes silent thrashing. Better to have 256 stable entries than 4096 with churn.
- Credit windows should be short (1-3s) to align with interactive user flows — avoids long-lived speculative workloads.
- Config should expose "aggressiveness" numeric 0..100 so server can tune without new schema changes.

Reference links / TODO fill-ins:
- copy-paste from earlier proposals: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy-runtime/pull/73 (PR with initial proto)
- add confluence write-up if we take to infra review: confluence:PROXY-RUNTIME-AXIOMS-2024

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally informal. Next session: pick one TODO and convert into a one-pager.
